observation.visible_scene: A black Sony 5-disc CD changer sits on a white surface with a sheet of paper on top. Its disc tray is fully extended, holding two CDs side by side: a silver disc labeled 'NATURESCAPES' on the left and a black disc labeled 'Beatles' on the right. The front display reads 'DISC-1'. The camera is essentially fixed on the unit.
visible_changes: During the early frames (approx. t=0 to t=0.46s) both discs on the open tray turn through a small angle (roughly 30-45 degrees), after which they remain stationary for the rest of the clip.
The rainbow diffraction pattern on the silver disc shifts in step with that rotation (a reflection change, not a new object).
From about t=2.0s a person's finger/hand enters from the right edge and rests on / presses the right-side control buttons, staying there until the last frame.
The tray stays open, the display continues to show 'DISC-1', and no other mechanical motion is visible during the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the discs came to be on the tray, and whether the disc rotation is a settling motion or part of a loading/indexing cycle.
What (if anything) the button press triggers after the clip ends (e.g. tray closing or disc selection), since no such result appears within the frames.
uncertain_details: Whether the finger actually depresses a button or merely hovers/contacts it.
The cause of the brief disc rotation; the excerpt shows the rotation itself but not its origin.
Any tiny camera jitter is negligible and the framing is treated as static.
